name: Chettinad Kozhi Biryani
subtitle: short-grain seeraga samba rice cooked with chicken, mint and whole spice

ingredients.note: the small aromatic Chettinad rice; basmati is a poor substitute here

prepNotes: Marinate the chicken in the yogurt, half the ginger-garlic paste, turmeric, chilli powder and salt for at least 1 hour, refrigerated.
Wash the seeraga samba in three changes of water and soak it 20 minutes only. It is a small grain and turns to porridge if soaked longer.
The ratio for seeraga samba is about 1.5 cups water to 1 cup rice, not the 2:1 you use for basmati. Measure the soaking water out separately.
Have every ingredient chopped before you start — once the rice goes in, the timing is fixed.

steps.text: Heat the ghee and gingelly oil together in a heavy pot. Fry the star anise, cinnamon, cloves, cardamom, bay leaf, mace, stone flower and fennel for 40 seconds, until they lift and smell sweet.
steps.tip: Whole spices first, in fat, on medium heat. Thrown in later they never release properly.

steps.text: Add the sliced onion and fry 12 minutes, until evenly deep gold. Keep a spoonful back for the top.
Stir in the remaining ginger-garlic paste, green chillies and curry leaves and fry 2 minutes.
Add the tomatoes, coriander powder and crushed pepper and cook 8 minutes, until the tomatoes have gone to pulp and oil shows at the sides.
Add the marinated chicken with all its yogurt and fry on high 6 minutes, until the yogurt tightens around the pieces and stops looking watery.
steps.tip: Cook the yogurt off properly or it splits later and leaves the rice sour and streaky.

steps.text: Throw in the mint and coriander leaves and cook 2 minutes, until they wilt into the masala.
Pour in 750ml water, add the lemon juice and salt, and bring to a hard boil. Taste it now — the liquid should be slightly saltier than you want the finished rice.
steps.tip: This is the only chance to correct seasoning. Once the rice is in, you cannot fix it.

steps.text: Drain the rice and stir it in. Boil uncovered on high until the water level drops to the surface of the rice, about 6 minutes.
Cover tightly, drop the heat to the lowest setting and cook 15 minutes without lifting the lid.
Turn off the heat and leave it covered another 10 minutes.
steps.tip: The rest is not optional. Opening early gives you wet grains at the bottom and dry ones on top.

steps.text: Fork through gently from the edges inward, top with the reserved fried onion and serve with onion raita and brinjal curry.

storage: Keeps 2 days refrigerated. Reheat portions covered with 1 tbsp water over low heat or in a steamer for 6 minutes; stirring hot biryani breaks the grains.
